svg.text: C1-F CHEST FREEZER ON A STAND, HATCH IN THE LID — cheapest freezer fallback
A chest is a top-access appliance by nature: B's slide sits on its lid, a turntable brings a stack under it, and the gallery digs.
no motor, wire or grease in the cold
static frost, no drain: fails CLD-008
dashed: the hatch (fixed); front is at the bottom
green = stack with the wanted box
a lid is a door: a window in it
cold air stays in the tub
static chest: rime on the walls,

g.text: 1/6 The wanted (green) box is second from the top of the stack under the hatch. The slide on the lid opens.
2/6 The gallery hoist digs: it lifts the box on top out through the hatch and holds it; the hatch closes.
3/6 With the hatch shut the turntable turns 90° (motor on the lid, shaft through the lid): another stack comes under the hatch.
4/6 The hatch opens again and the gallery sets the dug box down on that stack, then the turntable turns back.
5/6 Third pass: the gallery lifts the wanted box out. Cold air stays in the tub; the hatch is open about 3 s per pass.
6/6 The catch: a static chest frosts up and has no drain, and the 940 mm stand under it is lost for storage.
